# Explain predictive models {.unnumbered}

You have a forest fit, but the model itself is not the clinical explanation.
Start with whether it converged, then choose the slice that answers what it
predicts, which variables matter, and where a predictor changes the response.

## Choose the next recipe

| Your question | Recipe | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| Did the forest settle as more trees were grown? | [Random forest error convergence](rf_error.qmd) | Reads the out-of-bag error curve before interpreting the fit. |
| What does the forest predict for a patient or group? | [Predicted response and survival](rf_predicted.qmd) | Shows fitted responses and survival estimates. |
| Which predictors contribute most to the fit? | [Variable importance](rf_vimp.qmd) | Ranks variables by their contribution to prediction. |
| How did a variable contribute to an individual prediction? | [SHAP attribution](rf_shap.qmd) | Shows per-observation, per-variable attributions. |
| How does the predicted response change over a predictor? | [Variable and partial dependence](rf_dependence.qmd) | Draws marginal and partial effects. |
| How well does a classification forest discriminate and calibrate? | [ROC and Brier performance](rf_roc.qmd) | Gives ROC and Brier views of classification performance. |
| Which variables survive rule-based selection? | [Variable priority with varPro](varpro.qmd) | Shows the variable-priority workflow. |
| What does a selected variable do across its range? | [varPro partial dependence](varpro_partial.qmd) | Reads the partial effect after selection. |
| How do I inspect a forest with time-varying covariates? | [Random Hazard Forests](rf_rhf.qmd) | Uses start-stop data when predictors and risk change with time. |
